messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Paging: P95 latency SLO breach on runtime-canary (slice: canary-eu-west-1). Alert: p95=2.1s (>800ms), error-rate spike to 0.9%. Link: https://alerts.redwood.local/1743322099
alex_oncall: Ack. I’m on it — collecting context.
deploy-bot: FYI release '2026-03-17-rc5' completed canary rollout to 20% @ 1743300000. No automated rollback triggered.
priya_eng_runtime: seeing profiler traces — kernel selector fell back to generic-kernel on all canary pods, causing extra memcpy and high tail latency. Suspect the quantized-kernel path mis-registered for the new operator shape.
sam_sre: taking node-level metrics now. `top` shows high iowait on nodes running canary slice. Pulling out logs.
priya_eng_runtime: logs: ```ERROR kernel_selector.cpp:142 register_kernel: kernel mismatch for op=attention_v2, fallback=generic-kernel, reason=shape-mismatch```
alex_oncall: any quick rollback option? feature flag flip?
priya_eng_runtime: yes — we have a kill-switch: `ff.runtime.use_new_kernel_selector=false` in LaunchDarkly. Can flip to force previous kernel mapping. That should stop new selector from being used and allow running quant-kernel.
alex_oncall: flipping now. `ld toggles off ff.runtime.use_new_kernel_selector --env=prod --target=canary-eu-west-1`
deploy-bot: Feature flag update applied (ff.runtime.use_new_kernel_selector=false) — propagation ~30s.
priya_eng_runtime: confirming: restarted canary pods automatically picked up old mapping, kernel choice reverted on first warmup.
sam_sre: running synthetic probe: `curl -sS https://canary.runtime.redwood/api/health?probe=tail` -> before flip p95=2100ms, after flip p95=420ms. Improving.
emily_support: Support: two customers (acct-422, acct-998) reported increased response times and one transient 504. Escalated to SEs, CS notified. No major revenue hits flagged yet.
priya_eng_runtime: still seeing some tail errors from long sequences; appears KV-cache miss rate higher because some sessions re-warmed. Suggest reducing batch-window to reduce queuing for long-tail.
alex_oncall: can we adjust batching quickly?
priya_eng_runtime: yes. Pushing config change: `service.runtime.batch.window_ms: 8 -> 4` and disable continuous microbatching on canary: `service.runtime.batch.continuous=false`
sam_sre: applying canary config via runtime-config: `rdctl apply -f canary-batch-tweak.yaml --slice=canary-eu-west-1`
deploy-bot: Config applied, rolling restart of 12 canary pods started.
priya_eng_runtime: monitoring traces. Early signs: tail latency down further, throughput stable. Keep an eye on CPU % and token throughput.
emily_support: Customer comms: drafting note for acct-422/998, will state transient performance regression during canary rollout; advising retry/backoff.
maria_prod: quick customer-impact estimate: SLO exposure increment ~0.12% for the hour window, active error budget remaining ~0.18%. We'll need to include this in postmortem.
alex_oncall: current plan: 1) kill-switch flag on (done), 2) batch window tweak (done), 3) continue monitoring for 60m, 4) if stable, abort the rest of rollout and cut a rollback release for rc5. Priya, can you take lead for next hour? I need to handoff at 18:00 UTC.
priya_eng_runtime: taking lead. I’ll collect perf diffs and prepare rollback artifact if needed. Will keep both oncall and SRE looped.
sam_sre: added runbook note and increased alerting sensitivity for p99 > 1.5s.
emily_support: logged incidents in Zendesk, CS will follow up if customers need remediation credits.
alex_oncall: handing off to @priya_eng_runtime at 18:00 UTC. I’ll remain reachable for escalation.
priya_eng_runtime: accepted. Next update in 20m or on major status change.
incident-bot: Incident marked: severity=sev2, incident_id=INC-20260317-045. Handoff recorded: from alex_oncall -> priya_eng_runtime.
priya_eng_runtime: note for postmortem: root cause likely regressed kernel registration for attention_v2 when new quantized operator shape introduced in rc5. Action items: (1) revert kernel registry change, (2) add unit test for attention shapes, (3) tighten canary SLO gates for kernel selection regressions.
alex_oncall: thanks team. Closing the paging loop for now; monitoring continues.
